newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soybeans turn lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soybeans turn lower on profit taking.

text.p: CBOT new crop soybean futures turned lower in early trade on profit taking and commission house selling, traders said.
O'Connor and Co was said to be an early seller of at least two million bushels November.
Pit sources also noted commercial hedge selling as farmer selling of soy increased. Term Commodities and Produce Grain each sold one million bushels November, pit sources said.
Soymeal also turned lower, keying off of losses in soybeans.
Locals were said to be buyers on the break, with underlying support also coming from the August contract which rose on the lack of deliveries.
At 0946 CDT, soybeans were up 6-1/2 cents per bushel to unchanged with November up 1/2 at $6.56. Soymeal was up $1.20 per ton to down $0.60 with December down $0.60 at 216.00.
